title: The output buffer is sized for the input, but the transformation can expand a character and write more bytes than it read
index_line: T-0096 · MEM_WRITE · one-byte heap overflow in Ruby case conversion: ß→SS consumes the +20 slack · c · corroborated
invariant_violated: The converter assumed that case conversion preserves size: allocate the input length plus some slack, then one output byte per input byte. Character expansion breaks that — a single character can legitimately map to two — and the loop's per-iteration room check only ever reserved room for one.

mechanism.does: an attacker-supplied string in a legacy single-byte encoding (ISO-8859-x, Windows-125x) reaches upcase/swapcase/downcase(:fold)/casecmp?
the case-conversion loop walks the string and writes converted characters
a character with no uppercase form in that encoding (eszett) expands to two bytes (SS)
the loop's guard only ensures room for one byte, so the second byte is written unchecked; the buffer is input length + 20 and each expansion consumes one byte of slack
21 such characters write one byte past the buffer — a controlled 0x73 into the adjacent heap object, corrupting a length/pointer reachable for code execution

source.http.request.value: a request-supplied string in a legacy encoding that the application upcases/folds (headers, params, filenames)

size.length.value: the output buffer sized as input length + 20, and the per-iteration 'room for one byte' check

encoding.string.value: single-byte encodings whose case mapping expands one character into two

preconditions.expr: application code case-converts strings that arrive in a legacy encoding
the input can carry 0xDF (eszett) bytes in a single-byte encoding

check.spec: printf 'probe: send 21 x \xDF in ISO-8859-1/Windows-1252 then trigger case conversion\n'

success: a heap-corruption crash after case-converting a string containing 21+ eszett characters
a controlled single byte written past a string buffer, visible as a corrupted adjacent object
failure_like: the build is patched to reserve expansion room or to check each byte
UTF-8-only input paths (the expansion does not apply the same way)
false_positive: an encoding error is not this bug — require the specific expansion path and heap effect
a crash on invalid byte sequences may be the regexp CVEs from the same advisory batch, not this one

hazards: any text transform that can expand: case folding, transliteration, entity escaping, URL/percent encoding
the slack constant (+20) is the entire safety margin, so the number of expansions needed is tiny
single-byte legacy encodings are where the expansion rules are surprising
non_transfers: converters that grow the buffer or pre-compute the expanded length
languages whose case mapping is size-stable for the encodings in use
